messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: log_prob and grad_log_prob functions
parts:
Is there any way to evaluate the log joint probability of a data set and its gradient in rstan without creating a stan_fit object? It seems awkward that I have to do this

    sf <- sampling(my_stan_model, data=data, init=0, chains=1, iter=2)

just so that I can evaluate log_prob for various parameter vectors (via log_prob(sf, parameter_vector)).

BTW, the reason I ask is that I am using a simpler model to produce good starting points for a more complex model, and so I want to get both a MAP estimate and observed information matrix at that point. This is what I'm doing now:

    fit <- optimizing(my_stan_model, data=data, init=0)
    sf <- sampling(my_stan_model, data=data, init=0, chains=1, iter=2)
    info_matrix <- -fdHess(fit$par, function(x)log_prob(sf, x))$Hessian

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] log_prob and grad_log_prob functions
parts:
No.  One reason is that we added these functions later and a natural place to add is for stanfit object as the data have been read (and a model instance in terms of C++ that using Rcpp is created in memory, which is needed for these two functions).

--
Jiqiang

I converted this to a feature request on stan-dev/rstan:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/17

I also added a feature request to allow external .csv
files to be read in for posterior analysis Coda-style:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/18

Jiqiang --- I know these are non-trivial extension requests and
we realize we can't expect you to build everything in RStan.
I'm just using the issue tracker to store design ideas for the
future.

We need to recruit some more R developers.

- Bob
